payload.name: observer-controller
payload.scope: To implement state-space control when not all states are directly measurable, by combining a state estimator with a state-feedback law into a single dynamic compensator.

definition.body: observer-controller is a human-authored control design methodology that combines a state observer with a state-feedback controller, using the observer's estimated states as inputs to the feedback law so that a complete control system can be built when not all states are directly measurable. Parameters: (1) an observer (typically Luenberger or Kalman) that estimates the state vector from available measurements; (2) a feedback gain law (e.g. u = -Kx_hat) that drives the estimated states toward desired values; (3) the combined dynamics where the observer and controller eigenvalues are distinct and the control law acts on estimated rather than true states. It persists as the standard implementation pattern for state-space control in practice — whenever full state measurement is unavailable, the observer-controller architecture is the canonical solution — encoded in control engineering texts (Ogata's Modern Control Engineering; Chen, Linear System Theory), embedded in MATLAB's ctrlsynth toolchains, and deployed in aerospace, robotics, and process control systems. e.g.: Luenberger-based observer-controller for a DC-motor speed loop where only encoder feedback is available; Kalman-filter-based observer-controller for satellite attitude control using star tracker measurements; embedded observer-controller on a quadcopter flight controller using IMU measurements | not: full-state feedback (uses actual states directly, no observer); output-feedback (uses a static gain on outputs, not a dynamic observer) [formal: controlator observatorque | substrate: mind | horizon: centuries | explicit: yes]

payload.name: mu-synthesis
payload.scope: To design controllers that ensure robust performance against structured uncertainty by minimizing the structured singular value (mu) of the closed-loop system.

definition.body: mu-synthesis is a human-authored robust control design methodology that iteratively designs a controller to minimize the structured singular value (mu) of the closed-loop system across frequency, ensuring robust stability and performance against structured plant uncertainty. Parameters: (1) a generalized plant model with structured uncertainty blocks (delta) representing parametric variations and unmodeled dynamics; (2) D-K iteration: alternating between scaling matrices D (for mu minimization) and K-controller synthesis (H-infinity optimization for each iteration); (3) the structured singular value mu which quantifies the worst-case effect of the uncertainty structure on closed-loop performance. It persists as the premier method for robust control design with structured uncertainty in aerospace and high-performance systems, documented in canonical texts (Doyle, 'History of Robust Control'; Zhou, Doyle and Glover, 'Robust and Optimal Control'; Balakrishnan and Doyle) and implemented in MATLAB's mu synthesis and DK-synthesis toolboxes. e.g.: D-K iteration for a hypersonic vehicle flight control system with 20% thrust uncertainty blocks; mu-synthesized autopilot for an F-16 across a grid of flight conditions; robust guidance law for a reusable launch vehicle with mass and inertia uncertainties | not: H-infinity control (minimizes worst-case gain for unstructured uncertainty, not structured singular value); LMI-based robust control (convex optimization approach, not D-K iteration) [formal: synthetica valoris structurate singularis | substrate: mind | horizon: centuries | explicit: yes]

The observer is the computational heart of the architecture.
